summary.text: In March 2026 Senate testimony, Arvind Raman said that if confirmed he would help NIST deliver on the President’s AI action plan and maximize innovation across the American AI tech stack, and he called advancing leadership in chips a high priority. In the same testimony, he described NIST’s AI role as providing measurement science and frameworks for other agencies, and said he would work to continue NIST’s leadership in AI metrology if confirmed. In August 2026, as NIST Director, Raman said NIST’s contribution to the Genesis Mission exemplified its commitment to advancing U.S. leadership in critical technologies and that NIST was using public-private partnerships to apply advanced AI to manufacturing and cybersecurity. In 2024, before his NIST directorship, Raman was reported saying there was an urgent need for AI-equipped sensor networks to detect potential threats, and he was reported noting that the Institute of Chips and AI joined other Purdue programs focused on physical AI.
